chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Frances Wayne as the most ladylike singer
summary: Barnet and Willard remember Wayne as exceptionally ladylike compared with Lena Horne.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: She was one of the most remarkable people I ever knew, I think. Very, very special lady.

Oh, she was very much a lady. She just didn't fit the -- I'm not putting the gal singers down with the bands, but she's the most ladylike singer I ever had in my life. Now, I'm not saying that Lena Horne wasn't a lady, because she was. But you know, Lena could read somebody off if they came on too strong. But not Frances. Frances would just recoil in horror and gasp, you know.
But I think she could still handle things in her very lovely way.
Yeah. She always took care of things.
Nothing was beyond her, but she was different. It was a real privilege to know Frances, I think. Buddy De Franco.
